card.summary: no free tier and no setup fee; billing is hourly with a monthly cap, JPY 409 a month (JPY 449 with tax) for 1 GB, JPY 290 (JPY 319) for the IPv6-only 768 MB ...

free_tier.stated: no free tier and no setup fee; billing is hourly with a monthly cap, JPY 409 a month (JPY 449 with tax) for 1 GB, JPY 290 (JPY 319) for the IPv6-only 768 MB shape

retention.stated: the instance bills from creation to deletion, including while stopped: '停止中のインスタンスにも料金は発生します。'

egress.terms: no traffic volume quota stated; the port is capped at 100 Mbit/s on the 1 GB and 2 GB shapes and 500 Mbit/s on the 4 GB shape
egress.free_allowance: unlimited: no data transfer volume limit; port speed capped per shape; no overage price

record.interface_detail: The spec page documents a REST API (English-only API documentation at indigo.arena.ne.jp/userapi/, access token by POST to /oauth/v1/accesstokens) and public-key SSH login to instances.
record.tooling: No client library or CLI is named: the spec page and the API document at indigo.arena.ne.jp/userapi/ were read and describe the REST API with cURL examples only.
record.chaining: At JPY 0.48 an hour with no minimum term, a 768 MB instance costs about JPY 12 for a day, which is the cheapest way found in Japan to hold a reachable IPv6 box for a single job; the missing IPv4 pushes any client that needs one to the JPY 0.64 1 GB shape.

limits.value: 100 Mbit/s port on the 1 GB shape

record.limits_note: The entry shapes are capped at 100 Mbps and the 768 MB shape has no IPv4 address at all, so the first thing that fails is anything that needs a public IPv4 or a fast outbound path; the monthly floor of JPY 50 (JPY 55 with tax) is the second: a month with any usage at all costs at least that.
record.binding_note: the 100 Mbit/s port and the 20 GB disk bind before the traffic does; there is no traffic quota to run out of

identity_cost.detail: the signup flow is email verification, then SMS or automated-voice phone verification, then card registration: 'メール認証', 'SMSまたは電話認証', 'クレジットカード登録'. No charge is raised at card registration: 'クレジットカード登録時点で料金は発生しません。インスタンス作成後に料金が発生します。' A separate eKYC identity check exists whose accepted documents are all Japanese (driving licence, My Number card, residence card, a Japanese-issued passport); which signup paths require it was not established

record.notes: Prices on the page are shown pre-tax with the tax-inclusive figure in parentheses, and both are recorded. The 10 h/day figure uses the hourly rate because this product is billed hourly; the 24/7 figure is the monthly cap. The Japanese site is the only route; no English page was found.

extras.price_arithmetic: 24/7: 730 h x JPY 0.70 = JPY 511, above the JPY 449 monthly cap, so the cap binds: 449/156.839696 = USD 2.86. 10 h/day: 300 h x JPY 0.70 = JPY 210 = USD 1.34

record.binding_note: The 20-day window ends long before 1 TiB/month accumulates, and the machine is wiped rather than throttled. No byte allowance is published, so no volume quota can bind first.

identity_cost.detail: [translated] 'Fill in the necessary items on the application form and post it to the address given on the form.' There is no online signup for the trial: NTTPC issues a test-server ID within five business days of receiving the paper form.

record.reliability_note: The machine is stopped and initialised the day after the end notice and the data is unrecoverable by design; the trial is limited to verification work and may not be used as a live commercial site.
record.confidence_note: The 20-day term, the 4G specification, the postal application and the suspension are all on the vendor page read on 2026-10-23. A probe would establish the actual public address and rate; that requires an accepted application, which is currently impossible.

record.notes: A 4-core 4 GB Japanese guest for 20 days with no card would be the best trial shape, and it is closed twice over: the paper form is a postal step with a five-business-day turnaround, and the page read on 2026-10-23 says new applications are temporarily suspended, pointing at a news item dated 2026-10-21. identity_kind 'institution' is the closest token for a posted, signed form; the gate is process, not a national ID. Country: Japan (NTTPC Communications). WebARENA's other line, VPS Cloud, ended its trial on 2018-02-16 per its own page.
